meta.title: Open Pointcloud Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Desktop application for laser scans and point clouds (LAS, LAZ, E57): view, measure, convert, DXF and DWG section drawings, meshes. Windows, macOS, Linux.

header.label: View, measure and edit point clouds
header.title: Open Pointcloud Studio
header.tagline: From laser scan to dimension, drawing and mesh
header.desc: A desktop application for viewing, measuring, editing and converting laser scans and other point clouds. From a scan it makes a section drawing in DXF or DWG, a closed mesh, and the planes and cylinders of a room. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, is written in Rust and needs no browser or web view.

cta.related: See also Open CAD Studio, which comes in every package and shows the drawings

notice.text: First time? The guide takes you in a few steps from installing to your first section drawing. Go to the guide

features.label: Features
features.heading: From scan to drawing
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

project.title: A whole scan project at once

large.title: Large scans, on screen at once
large.desc: LAS and LAZ open from their header, a large E57 file first shows a sample, and from one million points on the application builds an index on disk. It supplies the detail for the current viewpoint, up to ten million points in view, and is kept for next time.

section.title: A section box that follows the walls
section.desc: Six draggable faces limit what you see, select, export and draw. Type the limits, or turn the box with Align to walls along a building that stands at an angle in the scan. Measure distances and areas, also of a wall or a sloped roof.

drawing.title: From scan to floor plan in DXF or DWG
drawing.desc: A section drawing makes a plan or section at scale 1:1 of what the box cuts. The filled cut draws walls, columns and floors as regions and leaves door and window openings open; straight CAD lines add editable polylines. Open CAD Studio comes with it and shows the result at once, and on a sheet with a title block you place views at scale for a PDF.

mesh.title: A closed mesh that tells you how good it is
mesh.desc: Put the box around a room and make a surface without overlaps, closed wherever the scan has points and with door and window openings left open. Afterwards you see the mean, the 95% and the largest distance between the points and the mesh. Export as OBJ, PLY, STL, DXF, DWG or IFC.

faces.title: Floors, walls and columns detected
faces.desc: Detect faces finds the flat faces of a room with their outlines, in which a window is a hole and a door a notch, and round columns and pipes as cylinders. For each face you see the type, the area and the residual of its points; export as JSON, OBJ, DXF, DWG or as IFC4 building elements.

open.desc: LAS, LAZ, E57, PLY, PCD, PTX, PTS and text, and meshes in OBJ, PLY, OFF and STL. Each file is a layer you show, hide or close.

project.desc: A folder of scans, or the scans a scan project file (.rcp) lists, open together. Dropping them on the window works too.

lod.desc: An index on disk (an octree) supplies the detail for the camera position; the points stay on screen while you move.

display.desc: Colour, elevation, intensity or class, eye-dome lighting, a view cube and perspective or orthographic.

photos.title: Station photos and panoramas
photos.desc: Stand in a scanner station, lay the photo over the points and give points the colours the photos see.

compare.title: Photo beside the 3D model
compare.desc: An E57 photo in a tab of its own, beside or above a 3D pane, with a draggable divider.

bag.desc: Download building models of the Netherlands for an area in RD coordinates and show them with your scan.

language.desc: The interface follows the language of the system and can be switched in Settings, with five colour themes.

measure.desc: Distance, horizontal length and height difference, and areas in their own plane, picked from all points of the scan.

section.title: Section box that turns
section.desc: Six draggable faces, typed limits and alignment to the walls; where it cuts a mesh, the cut looks solid.

edit.desc: Select with a rectangle, delete with undo, thin, move and scale. The source file never changes.

register.title: Register scans
register.desc: Align scans with point pairs or a manual shift, refined with ICP, with residuals and a preview in deviation colours.

export.desc: The whole cloud, the selection or the section box as LAS, LAZ, E57, PLY, XYZ, PTS or CSV, and merging scans of mixed formats.

views.desc: A view keeps the camera, the section box and the notes; all views of a scan go out as one BCF 2.1 file.

drawing.desc: Plan, elevation or section in DXF or DWG, with a filled cut and straight CAD lines on a layer of their own.

sheets.title: Sheets to PDF
sheets.desc: A4 to A0 with a title block, views at scale, dimensions and text, exported as a PDF the size of the sheet.

terrain.title: Terrain and 3D surface
terrain.desc: Quick meshes of a scan, also as an OBJ with a texture (MTL and PNG) from the measured colours.

closedMesh.desc: A surface without overlaps of a room, with the measured distance between the points and the mesh.

faces.desc: Floors, ceilings, walls, sloped faces and round columns, as JSON, OBJ, DXF, DWG or IFC4.

api.title: Command API
api.desc: Every window listens on 127.0.0.1 and runs commands from scripts and other programs, only with a token.

mcp.title: Works with an AI assistant
mcp.desc: The MCP server gives an assistant a tool for every command and a screenshot of the 3D view.

cli.title: Command line
cli.desc: Convert, cut, merge, draw, mesh and detect faces without a window.

library.title: C library and cloud API
library.desc: The point-cloud core for software of your own, as a C library or as a service over HTTP and MCP in a container.

ext.title: Extensions
ext.desc: Extra tasks by other authors, as a program in any language that drives the window through the command API.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v2026.45.1
download.lead: Free and without an account. Every button starts the download right away.
download.metaMac: Disk image for macOS 11 and later, Apple and Intel processors
download.metaLinux: AppImage for Linux x86-64, runs on most distributions
download.mobileNote: Open Pointcloud Studio is a desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux. Download it on your computer; all files are listed below.

note.signed: Windows and macOS: the installer installs for you alone, without administrator rights, or for all users. The release notes state for each version whether the files are signed; when the Mac app is notarised, macOS opens it without extra steps.
note.linux: Linux: make the AppImage executable once with chmod +x and then start it; without FUSE, start it with --appimage-extract-and-run after the file name. Install the .deb package with sudo apt install ./open-pointcloud-studio_*_amd64.deb. It needs a C library of version 2.35 or newer and the C++ runtime of GCC 12 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or later), X11 or Wayland, and a Vulkan driver or OpenGL ES 3.
note.arm: Linux on 64-bit ARM: experimental. These packages are built and tested only on build machines with software rendering, not yet on real ARM boards or laptops.
note.sha: In the release every file has a .sha256 file of the same name beside it, holding its checksum: put .sha256 after the address of a download to fetch it. The README describes how to check a download with it.
note.dev: For software of your own the same release carries the point-cloud core as a C library and, as a container image, the cloud API. See library.md and cloud-api.md.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.45.1
whatsnew.title: Photos, registration and merging
whatsnew.desc: Released on 3 November 2026. E57 photos are kept through every edit, and you can now align scans to each other in the application.

photos.title: Photos are kept
photos.desc: E57 exports keep station photos, panoramas, masks and camera poses, also after filtering, a section box export or colouring from photos.

photoEdit.title: Edit photos
photoEdit.desc: Add a panorama at a chosen point and camera height, or move, turn, rename or delete a photo, with undo.

register.title: Register scans
register.desc: Align with point pairs or a manual shift and rotation, refined with ICP, with residuals, a preview and a reusable transformation.

merge.title: Merge mixed formats
merge.desc: Merge visible scans of different formats into E57, LAS or LAZ; an E57 keeps the stations and photos.

api.title: API and MCP
api.desc: New commands for photos and registration, and the command line applies a saved registration to a full scan.

signing.title: Checkable offline
signing.desc: The release carries the public key, so you check the signatures without a keyserver.

cost.a: Nothing. Open Pointcloud Studio is open source: the desktop application is licensed under the GPL-3.0, the point-cloud core under the LGPL-3.0. No licence fees, no subscription and no account.

formats.a: LAS, LAZ, E57, PLY, PCD, PTX, PTS and text files with one point per line, and meshes in OBJ, PLY, OFF and STL. A folder of scans or a scan project file (.rcp) opens in one go; of such a project file only the list of scans is read, not the indexed scan copies (.rcs).

size.q: How large can a scan be?
size.a: For clouds of one million points or more, the application builds an index on disk. With it, scans of more than a hundred million points stay smooth: you see the detail of the current viewpoint, up to an adjustable maximum of ten million points in view. Such an index can take several gigabytes for a large survey.

cad.q: Can I use the results in my CAD or BIM program?
cad.a: Yes. Section drawings go to DXF or DWG, meshes and detected faces also as 3D geometry in DXF, DWG or IFC4, and saved views as BCF 2.1. Open CAD Studio comes in every package and shows an exported drawing at once. Opening DWG files is not possible.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows 10 and 11 (x64), macOS 11 and later on Apple and Intel processors, and Linux on x86-64 (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or later). The packages for Linux on 64-bit ARM are experimental. There is no browser version.

ai.q: Does it work with an AI assistant?
ai.a: Yes. open-pointcloud-studio --mcp starts an MCP server with a tool for every command of the local command API: open scans, set the section box, measure, export, draw and mesh, and send back the 3D view as an image.

library.q: Can I use the core in my own software?
library.a: Yes. The point-cloud core is available as a C library for Windows, macOS and Linux and as a cloud API in a container image, both under the LGPL-3.0. From Rust you use the crate directly.

lang.q: Which languages does the interface come in?
lang.a: Dutch and English. The application follows the language of the system; in Settings you switch the language and pick one of the five colour themes.

trust.q: How reliable are the section drawing, the closed mesh and face detection?
trust.a: They were measured on generated rooms, not yet on a scan of a real building. A closed mesh and detected faces report how far the points lie from them, so you can judge the result yourself. The known limits are listed on this page under Technology.

tech.heading: Formats, technology and licence
tech.sub: For those who want to know what goes in and out, and how it is built.

rust.title: Rust
rust.desc: One code base for Windows, macOS and Linux, without a browser or web view.

gpu.title: wgpu and iced
gpu.desc: 3D rendering on the GPU and an interface in the style of the OpenAEC desktop apps.

octree.title: Index on disk
octree.desc: An octree supplies the detail for each camera position and is kept for next time.

core.title: One core
core.desc: The command line, the cloud API and the C library (ABI 1.0) share the same operations.

api.title: Command API and MCP
api.desc: The server listens on the loopback address only and refuses a command without the token.

tech.desc: The desktop application is licensed under GPL-3.0-only, the point-cloud library under LGPL-3.0-or-later. Every package carries the licence texts.

formats.title: File formats
formats.las: Opens from the header; exports keep the original point records
formats.e57: Scanner positions, station photos, panoramas and photos taken along a path are read and can colour the points; exports keep them
formats.ply: Reads ASCII and little-endian binary; writes either
formats.ptx: With the scanner position of each scan
formats.text: Text with one point per line
formats.obj: Mesh with colours and normals; material colours are read, texture images are not. Also written with a texture (UV coordinates, MTL and PNG), and for detected faces with one group per face
formats.plyMesh: Shown as faces. Written as binary PLY with double-precision coordinates, and with colours and normals where the mesh has them
formats.stl: Shown as faces. Written as binary STL: triangles only, without colours. A mesh more than 2,048 m from zero is written relative to a whole-metre origin that the file header names
formats.off: Shown as faces; can be saved as OBJ, PLY, STL, DXF, DWG or IFC
formats.asDrawing: yes, as a drawing and in 3D
formats.dxf: Read: ASCII DXF only; POINT entities open as points, 3DFACE entities as faces. Written: the 2D drawing of a section box with points, filled regions and outlines, and in 3D detected faces and meshes. Not a format of the point exports
formats.dwg: As for DXF, in the versions R2004 to R2018 (3D in R2013). DWG files are not opened
formats.ifc: Detected faces and meshes as building elements with their measured values; faces with their openings, columns as extruded circles
formats.faces: The detected faces of a scan: every plane with its parameters, its outline and the residuals of its points, every cylinder with its axis, its radius and its residuals, and the edges between flat faces. The user guide describes every field
formats.rcp: Only the list of scans is read. The indexed scan copies (.rcs) of a project are a closed format and are not read
formats.bcf: Saved views with notes and pictures
formats.pdf: A sheet with its views, the size of the paper
formats.png: Picture of the 3D view, through the command API

limits.title: Good to know
limits.units: Lengths and areas are in metres. The coordinates of a scan are taken as metres and are not converted.
limits.measure: A measurement is not saved with the scan.
limits.surface: A 3D surface leaves holes and is not watertight.
limits.meshSize: A mesh holds at most four million vertices and eight million triangles, whether it comes from a file or from a mesh job.
limits.session: Detected faces are not saved with the scan: export them to keep them. A scan holds one mesh; a new mesh replaces the previous one.
limits.drawingPoints: The point limit of a section drawing is 150,000 points by default and at most 400,000; when thinning to 5 mm leaves more points, the point spacing doubles until they fit.
limits.fill: The filled cut of a section drawing is traced from the points: a wall scanned from one side is drawn as a thin strip, gaps under about half a metre are closed, and furniture in the slab is drawn unless its points are deleted first.
limits.closedMesh: A closed mesh rounds corners by about a quarter of a voxel, lets objects thinner than two or three voxels merge or get holes, and leaves some gaps beside another surface open. Without scanner stations, a surface that the centre of the region sees edge on can come out torn.
limits.faces: Detect faces reports no strips narrower than 0.15 m, such as door reveals. A region too large for the working budget is searched with larger voxels, thin scans give fewer faces or none, round columns wider than about 0.7 m come out as strips of wall, and without scanner stations the side a face looks at is a guess.
limits.generated: The filled cut, Closed mesh and Detect faces were measured on generated rooms, not yet on a scan of a real building. The user guide lists the limits of the filled cut, Closed mesh and Detect faces.
limits.index: An index can take several gigabytes on disk for a large survey.
